_README: OgreBot Classic -> OgreBot conversion map, read by ogre_convert.py (keep the two files in the same folder). GENERATED from the bot itself - do not edit by hand. One row per Classic name. Row fields: oldCall / oldName = the Classic spelling; status = what happened to it (argOrder | dataFile | moved | notPorted | portedElsewhere | removed | renamed | signature | stub | unchanged); newForm = what to write instead; oldSignature / newSignature = the old and new arguments (fw = the for-who, which comes first); oldSpellingToday = what the old spelling does under the new bot; howToFix = what to do; note = the traps; example = a real Classic line and its new-bot form; v2Row / v2Params = a console command's new row and its parameters in order. newApi / newConsole / newOgre list every name the new bot has; oldBotUnmapped lists Classic globals no row covers yet (any use is a question); idioms are Classic expressions that read differently now.

idioms.howToFix: Write ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.IsReady} - TRUE while OgreBot is up with a profile (paused or not, main window hidden or not).
Write ${ISXOgreEQ2.IM.IsOpen} - TRUE while the inventory manager window is up (${ISXOgreEQ2.IM.IsRunning} = it is working right now).

Drop the check and run `ogre cl` (Craft Lite) - it turns the crafting reactions ON, and doing that when they are already on changes nothing. ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Running} says whether a craft run is in progress.
Delete the check - Classic's nav test window is not in the new bot.
Write ${OgreConsoleHub.Sessions.Watching} - TRUE while the uplink's session watch is on. These scripts run in the uplink, where the hub is.
Write OgreConsoleHub.Sessions:On (in the uplink) - it turns the session watch on until the uplink restarts. To keep it on for good, tick Session watch on the EverQuest 2 tab of ogre config.

Attach to OgreEvent_SessionFrozen - same two arguments (session, uplink), fired in the uplink. It fires ONCE per freeze (OgrePing fired every round), so act on the first one; drop any timeout counter. A session that CLOSES or crashes now fires OgreEvent_SessionGone (OgrePing never reported those - scripts polled ${Session["isN"](exists)}), and a frozen one that comes back fires OgreEvent_SessionRecovered.
A Classic tool checked by its SCRIPT name - the new bot's tools are not LavishScript scripts, so this reads NULL. Stop and ask what replaces it.

newApi.OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget:AddActor: [fw, name, minHP, checkCollision, aggroOnGroupOnly, maxHP, aggroOnNonFighterOnly, aggroOnNotMe]

rows.note: Verified for the NON-persisted tab too, which is the one place this could have needed a second door: the shipped adapter already reads `checkbox_donotsave_dynamiccampspot` through `OgreBot::Value`. **THREE TRAPS.** (1) The bare `.<name>` form is NOT always a setting - the tab objects also carry METHODS (`IsCurePotionAvailable`, `AutoCastCurePotion`, `CanCastAbility`, `GetSetConvert`, ...). Only names with a control-id prefix (`checkbox_` / `combobox_` / `textentry_` / `slider_` / `listbox_`) are settings; converting a method to `.Value` silently yields "" == FALSE. (2) An ABSENT key reads `""`, which is FALSE - safe for an opt-IN checkbox, but an **opt-OUT** checkbox then fails OPEN and the feature switches itself on. State the default explicitly. (3) The value is TEXT (`"TRUE"`), not a bool - `CfgOn(v) { return v == "TRUE"; }`. **KEY COVERAGE (measured over CONSUMER files only - encounter content and instance controllers, excluding Classic's own `AutoIncludes`): 43 of 50 ids, 164 of 178 reads = 92%.** All SEVEN uncovered ids were checked individually and only ONE is a real gap: `combobox_extra_groupcure1` / `2` (6 reads) are **already dead in Classic** - the whole `Extras` tab is commented out of `object_TabInf_Base`, so those reads return NULL there today; `checkbox_settings_namedcombatarts` (3 reads) is likewise **stale** - the control survives only in 2013-era archived save XMLs, not in the current GUI; `OBUI_checkbox_donotsave_dynamiccampspot` is an **Classic bug** - the `OBUI_` UI-ELEMENT HANDLE passed where the settings KEY belongs; the 26 other sites use the plain `checkbox_donotsave_dynamiccampspot`, which IS covered. Converting a script that needs them needs that decision revisited, not a mapping. **Renames exist, so do not conclude 'absent' from the schema alone, and never match by name similarity:** `checkbox_debug_castingdetails` is `checkbox_debug_casting` on the new bot, while a fuzzy match proposes `checkbox_debug_castingextras`, a different control.
